scenarioStory.history: 34-week pregnant female (G2P1) with no prior seizure history. Husband reports a roughly 1-hour prodrome of severe headache and visual disturbances (spots), followed by a witnessed generalized tonic-clonic seizure lasting approximately 90 seconds. Patient is now postictal, confused, and continues to report headache. No prior history of hypertension or pre-eclampsia in this or a prior pregnancy.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 28-year-old pregnant female postictal on the living room floor after a witnessed generalized seizure. She is confused, severely hypertensive, and reports a headache that preceded the event. → Eclampsia recognized, magnesium given: Crew treats the seizure as eclampsia: IV access is obtained, magnesium sulfate is administered, supplemental oxygen is applied, and the patient is positioned in the left lateral position to optimize uterine perfusion. → DTRs reassessed, transport initiated: With reflexes and respiratory status confirmed normal, the crew continues the magnesium infusion, treats persistent severe hypertension, and initiates emergent transport with serial vital signs.

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 28-year-old pregnant female postictal on the living room floor after a witnessed generalized seizure. She is confused, severely hypertensive, and reports a headache that preceded the event.
relatedChecklist: Recognize new seizure at 34 weeks gestation as eclampsia until proven otherwise
Establish IV access; administer O2 to target 94-98% saturation
Position patient left lateral or manually displace uterus to the left
Magnesium sulfate 6 g IV over 5-10 min for seizure management

scenarioEvents.name: Eclampsia recognized, magnesium given
scenarioEvents.description: Crew treats the seizure as eclampsia: IV access is obtained, magnesium sulfate is administered, supplemental oxygen is applied, and the patient is positioned in the left lateral position to optimize uterine perfusion.
relatedChecklist: Reassess deep tendon reflexes and respiratory status after magnesium bolus
Continue magnesium sulfate maintenance infusion at 2 g/hr
Labetalol 20 mg IV over 2 minutes for persistent severe hypertension

scenarioEvents.name: DTRs reassessed, transport initiated
scenarioEvents.description: With reflexes and respiratory status confirmed normal, the crew continues the magnesium infusion, treats persistent severe hypertension, and initiates emergent transport with serial vital signs.
relatedChecklist: Repeat blood pressure and vital signs every 10 minutes during transport
Transport emergently to closest appropriate receiving facility; notify en route

scenarioEvents.name: Magnesium delayed, transport prioritized
scenarioEvents.description: Without magnesium sulfate on board, seizure prophylaxis is absent during transport. The patient has a second generalized convulsive seizure en route.
relatedChecklist: Midazolam 4 mg IV (78 kg x 0.1 mg/kg = 7.8 mg -> cap at 4 mg max) for recurrent seizure

scenarioEvents.name: DTRs not reassessed
scenarioEvents.description: The magnesium infusion continues unchecked. Deep tendon reflexes are lost, the patient becomes increasingly somnolent, and respirations slow — early signs of magnesium toxicity progressing toward respiratory paralysis.
relatedChecklist: Recognize absent DTRs, somnolence, and slurred speech as magnesium toxicity
Stop the magnesium sulfate infusion immediately
Calcium gluconate 3 g IV to reverse magnesium toxicity; support respirations
